title: Distinguishing Tics and Functional Tics Using Clinical Neurophysiological Techniques
sponsor: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS)
study_type: Observational; prospective cohort as registered, with physiological assessment over 1–2 days
population: Adults aged 18–80 with motor tics or functional motor tics; healthy-control group described
comparator: Motor-tic, functional-tic, and healthy-control groups; no treatment comparison
primary_outcome: Pre-tic EEG beta power at the vertex, registered time frame 2 days
exploratory_outcomes: EEG power in other frequency bands
novelty: An in-window registry posting to an existing study, deduplicated across two queries; not a newly registered trial or published result. Exact field changes from the preceding version were not verified.
limitations: Non-probability sample; selected adult physiology groups do not represent every age or severity.
Major psychiatric illness, depression/anxiety thresholds, tic-suppressing medication timing and low-urge eligibility criteria narrow applicability to sustained high-burden treated populations.
healthyVolunteers is false in structured API data although the arm and narrative explicitly seek healthy controls.
Vocal-tic-only wording in the exclusion list is ambiguous; do not infer eligibility beyond the explicit adult motor-tic criteria.
Recruiting status and future estimated start are separate fields; recruitment does not prove participant testing has begun.
Study design is not a long-term natural-history or treatment-benefit comparison.
claim_supported: NINDS has an updated registered adult physiological comparison targeting differences between motor and functional tics; no outcomes are posted.
claim_not_supported: Validated diagnostic biomarker, treatment efficacy, durable benefit, disease modification, or cure.
retrieval_status: Official ClinicalTrials.gov API current record inspected; official NIH search-indexed protocol corroborates recruitment/design. History web view inaccessible, so no specific field-change attribution.
next_verification_task: Inspect future posted results or a materially informative registry revision; do not infer outcomes from estimated dates.
privacy: Public aggregate protocol metadata only; no participant records or outreach.
